sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Datetime Module - Comprehensive Examples

```python
"""
Datetime Module - Comprehensive Examples
========================================
"""

from datetime import datetime, date, time, timedelta, timezone
import time as time_module

print("=" * 70)
print("DATETIME MODULE EXAMPLES")
print("=" * 70)

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 1: Creating datetime Objects
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 1: Creating datetime Objects")
print("=" * 70)

# Current datetime
now = datetime.now()
print(f"Current datetime: {now}")

# Specific datetime
dt = datetime(2024, 12, 25, 10, 30, 45)
print(f"Specific datetime: {dt}")

# From timestamp
timestamp = 1705328445.0
dt_from_ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(timestamp)
print(f"From timestamp {timestamp}: {dt_from_ts}")

# From ISO format
iso_string = "2024-01-15T14:30:45"
dt_from_iso = datetime.fromisoformat(iso_string)
print(f"From ISO '{iso_string}': {dt_from_iso}")

# UTC time
utc_now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
print(f"Current UTC time: {utc_now}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 2: Date Operations
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 2: Date Operations")
print("=" * 70)

today = date.today()
print(f"Today: {today}")
print(f"Year: {today.year}, Month: {today.month}, Day: {today.day}")
print(f"Weekday (0=Mon): {today.weekday()}")
print(f"ISO Weekday (1=Mon): {today.isoweekday()}")

# Date arithmetic
tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
yesterday = today - timedelta(days=1)
next_week = today + timedelta(weeks=1)

print(f"Tomorrow: {tomorrow}")
print(f"Yesterday: {yesterday}")
print(f"Next week: {next_week}")

# Date difference
birthday = date(1990, 5, 15)
age_days = (today - birthday).days
age_years = age_days // 365
print(f"Days since birthday: {age_days}")
print(f"Approximate age: {age_years} years")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 3: Time Operations
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 3: Time Operations")
print("=" * 70)

# Creating time objects
morning = time(9, 0, 0)
afternoon = time(14, 30, 0)
evening = time(18, 45, 30, 123456)  # with microseconds

print(f"Morning: {morning}")
print(f"Afternoon: {afternoon}")
print(f"Evening: {evening}")
print(
    f"Evening components: {evening.hour}h {evening.minute}m {evening.second}s {evening.microsecond}μs"
)

# Combining date and time
dt_combined = datetime.combine(today, morning)
print(f"Combined datetime: {dt_combined}")

# Extracting time from datetime
current_time = now.time()
print(f"Current time only: {current_time}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 4: timedelta Arithmetic
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 4: timedelta Arithmetic")
print("=" * 70)

# Creating timedeltas
one_day = timedelta(days=1)
one_week = timedelta(weeks=1)
two_hours = timedelta(hours=2)
mixed = timedelta(days=7, hours=3, minutes=30, seconds=15)

print(f"One day: {one_day}")
print(f"One week: {one_week}")
print(f"Mixed: {mixed}")
print(f"Mixed total seconds: {mixed.total_seconds()}")

# Arithmetic with datetime
meeting_time = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 14, 0, 0)
reminder_time = meeting_time - timedelta(hours=1)
follow_up = meeting_time + timedelta(days=7)

print(f"Meeting: {meeting_time}")
print(f"Reminder (1h before): {reminder_time}")
print(f"Follow-up (7 days after): {follow_up}")

# Difference between datetimes
start = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0)
end = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 15, 30, 45)
duration = end - start

print(f"Duration: {duration}")
print(f"Days: {duration.days}, Seconds: {duration.seconds}")
print(f"Total seconds: {duration.total_seconds()}")
print(f"Total hours: {duration.total_seconds() / 3600:.2f}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 5: String Formatting (strftime)
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 5: String Formatting (strftime)")
print("=" * 70)

dt = datetime(2024, 7, 4, 14, 30, 45)

formats = {
    "ISO format": dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    "US format": dt.strftime("%m/%d/%Y"),
    "Full text": dt.strftime("%A, %B %d, %Y"),
    "12-hour time": dt.strftime("%I:%M %p"),
    "Custom": dt.strftime("%b %d '%y at %I:%M%p"),
}

for name, formatted in formats.items():
    print(f"{name:15s}: {formatted}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 6: String Parsing (strptime)
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 6: String Parsing (strptime)")
print("=" * 70)

date_strings = [
    ("2024-01-15", "%Y-%m-%d"),
    ("01/15/2024", "%m/%d/%Y"),
    ("January 15, 2024", "%B %d, %Y"),
    ("15-Jan-2024 14:30", "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M"),
]

for date_str, format_str in date_strings:
    parsed = datetime.strptime(date_str, format_str)
    print(f"'{date_str}' -> {parsed}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 7: Timezone Handling
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 7: Timezone Handling")
print("=" * 70)

# UTC timezone
utc_dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
print(f"UTC time: {utc_dt}")

# Custom timezone (e.g., EST = UTC-5)
est = timezone(timedelta(hours=-5))
est_dt = datetime.now(est)
print(f"EST time: {est_dt}")

# IST (UTC+5:30)
ist = timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))
ist_dt = datetime.now(ist)
print(f"IST time: {ist_dt}")

# Convert between timezones
utc_time = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 20, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
est_time = utc_time.astimezone(est)
ist_time = utc_time.astimezone(ist)

print(f"UTC: {utc_time}")
print(f"EST: {est_time}")
print(f"IST: {ist_time}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 8: Calculate Age
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 8: Calculate Age")
print("=" * 70)
```

sections.title: calculate_age(), add_business_days()
sections.body:
Calculate age from birthdate Add business days (Mon-Fri) to a date

```python
def calculate_age(birthdate: date) -> int:
    """Calculate age from birthdate"""
    today = date.today()
    age = today.year - birthdate.year
    # Adjust if birthday hasn't occurred this year
    if (today.month, today.day) < (birthdate.month, birthdate.day):
        age -= 1
    return age

birthdates = [
    date(1990, 5, 15),
    date(2000, 12, 31),
    date(1985, 3, 20),
]

for bday in birthdates:
    age = calculate_age(bday)
    print(f"Born on {bday}: {age} years old")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 9: Business Days Calculation
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 9: Business Days Calculation")
print("=" * 70)

def add_business_days(start_date: date, days: int) -> date:
    """Add business days (Mon-Fri) to a date"""
    current = start_date
    added = 0

    while added < days:
        current += timedelta(days=1)
        # Check if it's a weekday (0=Mon, 6=Sun)
        if current.weekday() < 5:
            added += 1

    return current
```

sections.title: count_business_days(), date_range(), time_function()
sections.body:
Count business days between two dates Generate dates in a range Measure function execution time

```python
def count_business_days(start_date: date, end_date: date) -> int:
    """Count business days between two dates"""
    count = 0
    current = start_date

    while current <= end_date:
        if current.weekday() < 5:
            count += 1
        current += timedelta(days=1)

    return count

start = date(2024, 1, 15)  # Monday
result = add_business_days(start, 5)
print(f"Start date: {start} ({start.strftime('%A')})")
print(f"After 5 business days: {result} ({result.strftime('%A')})")

# Count business days
start_date = date(2024, 1, 1)
end_date = date(2024, 1, 31)
biz_days = count_business_days(start_date, end_date)
print(f"Business days in January 2024: {biz_days}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 10: Date Ranges
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 10: Date Ranges")
print("=" * 70)

def date_range(start: date, end: date):
    """Generate dates in a range"""
    current = start
    while current <= end:
        yield current
        current += timedelta(days=1)

print("First week of January 2024:")
for day in date_range(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 7)):
    print(f"  {day} - {day.strftime('%A')}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 11: Performance Measurement
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 11: Performance Measurement")
print("=" * 70)

def time_function(func, *args, **kwargs):
    """Measure function execution time"""
    start = datetime.now()
    result = func(*args, **kwargs)
    end = datetime.now()
    duration = end - start
    return result, duration
```

result, duration = time_function(slow_function)

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 12: Working with Timestamps")
print("=" * 70)

# Current timestamp
current_ts = time_module.time()
print(f"Current Unix timestamp: {current_ts:.2f}")

# Convert to datetime
dt_from_ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(current_ts)
dt_from_ts_utc = datetime.fromtimestamp(current_ts, tz=timezone.utc)
print(f"Local datetime: {dt_from_ts}")
print(f"UTC datetime: {dt_from_ts_utc}")

# Convert datetime to timestamp
dt = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
ts = dt.timestamp()
print(f"Timestamp of {dt}: {ts}")

# Millisecond timestamps (JavaScript style)
ms_timestamp = int(current_ts * 1000)
print(f"Millisecond timestamp: {ms_timestamp}")

# Convert from milliseconds
dt_from_ms = datetime.fromtimestamp(ms_timestamp / 1000)
print(f"From milliseconds: {dt_from_ms}")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("All examples completed!")
print("=" * 70)
